newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra Losec Europe sales worry analysts.
newsitem.headline: Astra Losec Europe sales worry analysts.

text.p: Drug sector analysts said on Tuesday that weak sales development in Europe for Swedish company Astra's number one drug Losec was the main factor behind the group's lower-than-expected first quarter result.

Analysts said it was anti-ulcer treatment Losec's sales performance, and not the effects of stockpiling late last year, that raised concerns and could cause some analysts to downgrade their forecasts for Astra in Europe.
"The result was clearly a disappointment... but one-off stockpiling and currency effects, we shouldn't worry too much about," said analyst Janet Dyson from Merrill Lynch.
"But I am worried about some of the trends for Losec in Europe."
Stefan Wikholm of Handelsbanken sais Astra needs to improve perfomance to keep its reputation as a high-growth company.
"We expected the numbers to be better but you need to remember that this is only one quarter, Wikholm said.
"Astra needs to show better growth during the rest of 1997 to avoid being classified as a normal drugs company."
He said lowering of analysts' estimates were to be expected.
Astra on Monday posted a one percent rise in first quarter profits to 3.46 billion crowns against market expectations of 3.93 billion crowns.
Sales rose nine percent to 10.13 billion crowns while Losec sales increased 14 percent to 4.80 billion crowns.
In Europe sales increased by just one percent to 5.6 billion crowns while North American sales increased to 2.94 billion crowns from 2.46 billion crowns.
The company said stockpiling by patients and wholesalers prior to year-end 1996 had wiped 400 million crowns off sales revenue.
But some analysts were not satisfied with that explanation.
"Even if you add in the 400 million crowns that stockpiling was estimated to have cost sales, you still expected sales to have been a bit better," said one analyst.
He said Astra's dependence on Losec was worrying.
"The company is sensitive to price pressure," he said.
Shares in Astra slumped 22 crowns on Monday. On Tuesday shares fell 10 at the open to 310.5 crowns but were also trading without a four crown dividend, and were nine crowns lower in afternoon trade.
